input.candidate_text:
The smallest value is \(\boxed{11}\).

For necessity, let the first player write
\[
25,25,25,25,23,22,22,22,22.
\]
Their sum is \(211\). The full list has sum \(211\), while every proper sublist omits at least one number, all of which are at least \(22\), and therefore has sum at most \(211-22=189\). Thus no sublist has sum in \([190,210]\). Hence \(N=10\), and consequently every \(N\le 10\), can fail.

It remains to prove that \(N=11\) always works. Given any finite list of positive integers at most \(25\) whose total is at least \(200\), repeatedly delete terms while the remaining sum is still at least \(200\). This produces an inclusion-minimal sublist \(B\) with sum
\[
T=200+r,\qquad r\ge0.
\]
For every \(b\in B\), minimality gives \(T-b<200\), so \(b>r\). Let \(m\) be the smallest element of \(B\). The second player can choose either all of \(B\), whose sum differs from \(200\) by \(r\), or \(B\setminus\{m\}\), whose sum differs from \(200\) by \(m-r\). We prove
\[
\min(r,m-r)\le11.
\]
Otherwise, \(r\ge12\) and \(m-r\ge12\). Since \(m\le25\), this forces \(12\le r\le13\).

If \(r=12\), then \(T=212\) and every element of \(B\) is at least \(24\). With at most eight elements the sum is at most \(8\cdot25=200\), while with at least nine elements it is at least \(9\cdot24=216\), both impossible.

If \(r=13\), then \(T=213\) and every element is at least \(25\), hence every element equals \(25\); their sum cannot be \(213\).

Therefore \(\min(r,m-r)\le11\), so one of the two indicated sublists has sum in \([189,211]\). Thus \(N=11\) is sufficient, and the counterexample proves it is minimal.
input.theorem: Let \( N \) be a positive integer. Two persons play the following game. The first player writes a list of positive integers not greater than \( 25 \), not necessarily different, such that their sum is at least \( 200 \). The second player wins if he can select some of these numbers so that their sum \( S \) satisfies the condition \( 200-N \leq S \leq 200+N \). What is the smallest value of \( N \) for which the second player has a winning strategy?
